title: A Wearable Continuous Immune Monitor: Shana Kelley on The Long Run - TimmermanReport.com
gist: Podcast intro: Chan Zuckerberg Biohub Chicago, led by Northwestern chemist Shana Kelley, is developing a continuous wearable immune/inflammation monitor modeled on continuous glucose monitors; inflammatory-protein detection was shown in mice (Science, Dec 2024) and commercialization will need an industry partner. Thin piece, largely sponsor copy.

insights.claim: Chan Zuckerberg Biohub Chicago, led by Northwestern chemist Shana Kelley, is developing a continuous wearable immune monitor for tracking inflammation, a device category that does not exist today.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Signals a potential new diagnostics/wearables category for inflammation; watch for spinouts or licensing deals.
insights.quote: No such device exists today for continuous tracking of inflammation.
insights.locator: One of the cool projects she oversees

insights.claim: The wearable immune monitor is explicitly modeled on continuous glucose monitors, which changed how diabetes is treated and managed, suggesting a CGM-like trajectory for immune disorders if it works.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: CGM precedent offers a template for market sizing and adoption of continuous inflammation sensing.
insights.quote: It’s inspired by continuous glucose monitors that have changed the way diabetes is treated and managed.
insights.locator: One of the cool projects she oversees

insights.claim: Successful continuous inflammation monitoring would have large implications for research and treatment of immune disorders affecting millions of people.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Could reshape immunology trial endpoints and disease management if technically proven.
insights.locator: One of the cool projects she oversees

themes.theme: Development stage and path to market

insights.claim: Detection of inflammatory proteins by the Kelley team's sensing approach has so far been demonstrated only in mice, with results published in Science in December 2024.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Preclinical stage only; human validation and commercialization are years away.
insights.quote: The detection of inflammatory proteins was demonstrated in mice and published in Science in December 2024.

insights.claim: Bringing the continuous immune monitor to market will require an industry partnership, creating a potential licensing or collaboration opportunity for diagnostics/medtech companies.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Watch for a medtech/diagnostics partner announcement as the commercialization catalyst.
insights.quote: The next steps to build something suitable for the marketplace will require some kind of industry partnership.
